text: Staying safe online is crucial to protect your personal data, finances, and digital identity. Here are essential safety practices ("parasites" can be corrected as "practices") to follow:
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats

locations.heading: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats

text:
- Create complex passwords using a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols.
- Avoid using the same password for multiple sites.
- Use a trusted password manager to store your credentials.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 1. Use Strong, Unique Passwords

text: - Add an extra layer of security with 2FA on all important accounts (email, banking, social media).
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 2. Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

text:
- Don’t click on suspicious links or download attachments from unknown sources.
- Double-check email addresses and URLs for authenticity.
- Never share personal information over email or phone unless you initiated contact.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 3. Beware of Phishing Scams

text: - Regularly update your operating system, apps, browsers, and antivirus programs to patch vulnerabilities.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 4. Keep Software Up to Date

text:
- Use a screen lock (PIN, password, or fingerprint) on smartphones and computers.
- Install trusted antivirus and anti-malware software.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 5. Secure Your Devices

text:
- Avoid public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions; use a VPN when needed.
- Only enter personal or financial information on websites with HTTPS.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 6. Use Secure Connections

text:
- Review statements regularly for unauthorized transactions.
- Set up instant alerts for account activity.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 7. Monitor Bank and Credit Accounts

text:
- Limit what information you share on social media and adjust privacy controls.
- Be wary of apps requesting unnecessary permissions.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 8. Manage Privacy Settings

text: - Regularly backup your files to a secure cloud service or external device.
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 9. Backup Important Data

text:
- Learn about new and emerging online threats.
- Participate in cybersecurity awareness programs.
Stay alert and proactive. Safe online habits protect your identity, money, and peace of mind!
path: Safety Practices to Protect Yourself from Online Threats > 10. Educate Yourself & Stay Informed
